scenarios.name: vectors/keys-z32-sign
scenarios.description: Go verifies endpoint IDs, z-base-32 encodings, signatures, and signed packets generated by Rust, and a pass proves byte-compatible key and signature representations.

scenarios.name: vectors/postcard-varints
scenarios.description: Go decodes postcard integer encodings generated by Rust, and a pass proves byte-compatible varint serialization at the tested boundaries.

scenarios.name: vectors/postcard-8bit
scenarios.description: Go encodes u8 and i8 values and compares them to the Rust driver's output at 0, 1, 127, 128, 200, 255 and -128, -2, -1, 0, 127, and a pass proves that both write a single raw byte rather than a varint above the 128 boundary.

scenarios.name: vectors/endpoint-ticket-roundtrip
scenarios.description: Go decodes and re-encodes endpoint tickets generated by Rust, and a pass proves a byte-identical ticket round trip.

scenarios.name: vectors/pkarr-txt
scenarios.description: Go verifies and parses a Rust-generated signed pkarr TXT packet, and a pass proves compatible packet signatures and TXT payload encoding.

scenarios.name: vectors/gossip-frame
scenarios.description: Go and the Rust test driver exchange framed gossip broadcasts in both directions, and a pass proves compatible topic, sender, and payload encoding.

scenarios.name: vectors/custom-addr-ticket-rust-to-go
scenarios.description: Go decodes CustomAddr endpoint tickets generated by Rust at lengths 0, 1, 29, 30, 31, and 255, and a pass proves Rust-to-Go compatibility across the inline-storage boundary.

scenarios.name: vectors/bao-range-proofs
scenarios.description: Go encodes range proofs for blobs of 0 to 300000 bytes and compares them to bao-tree's for whole blobs, the last chunk, chunk ranges inside, across, and past a 16-chunk block, and two spans in one block, then verifies bao-tree's encodings, and a pass proves go-iroh serves and accepts the partial-block proofs iroh-blobs does.

scenarios.name: vectors/bao-chunk-ranges
scenarios.description: Go produces and verifies bao-tree's range proofs for chunk ranges no byte range expresses: two spans in one block, the chunk at infinity, and ranges starting past the end, which iroh-blobs sends to ask for a size proof, and a pass proves go-iroh serves any range iroh-blobs can request.

scenarios.name: vectors/ip-ticket-rust-to-go
scenarios.description: Go decodes endpoint tickets generated by Rust that hold one IPv6 address, two, IPv4 and IPv6 together, IPv6 with a relay, and an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address, and a pass proves Go reads the (ip, port) form serde writes for a SocketAddrV6.

scenarios.name: vectors/ip-ticket-go-to-rust
scenarios.description: Rust decodes the same five endpoint tickets encoded by Go, and a pass proves Rust recovers the same addresses and relay and re-encodes them to Go's bytes.

scenarios.name: vectors/custom-addr-ticket-go-to-rust
scenarios.description: Rust decodes CustomAddr endpoint tickets generated by Go at lengths 0, 1, 29, 30, 31, and 255, and a pass proves Go-to-Rust compatibility across the inline-storage boundary.

scenarios.name: vectors/postcard-varint-strictness
scenarios.description: Go and the Rust driver decode the same canonical and non-canonically padded varint byte strings, and the recorded verdict is that they diverge: go-iroh rejects the padded encodings that postcard 1.1.3 accepts.
